purpose: Methylphenidate is used to help people with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) stay focused, control their impulses, and reduce hyperactivity. It is also sometimes used to treat narcolepsy, a condition that causes excessive daytime sleepiness. This medication can help both children and adults manage their ADHD symptoms so they can do better at school, work, and in daily life.
how_it_works: Your brain uses chemical messengers called dopamine and norepinephrine to help with focus and self-control. In people with ADHD, these chemicals are not as active as they should be. Methylphenidate works by boosting the levels of these chemicals in the brain, which helps improve attention, focus, and the ability to control behavior.
common_side_effects: Decreased appetite or not feeling hungry, especially around lunchtime. Trouble falling asleep if taken too late in the day. Headaches, stomachaches, or nausea. Feeling nervous, jittery, or irritable. A slightly faster heart rate or higher blood pressure. Some children may grow a little more slowly while on this medication, so their doctor will monitor their height and weight.
warnings: Do not take this medication if you have a heart condition, high blood pressure, or a history of heart problems without first talking to your doctor. It can be habit-forming, so take it exactly as prescribed and do not share it with others. Tell your doctor if you or a family member has a history of mental health issues, tics, or Tourette syndrome. Avoid taking it late in the afternoon or evening as it can cause insomnia. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: Dosing is different for everyone and depends on your age, weight, and which form of the medication you are taking. Short-acting tablets like regular Ritalin are usually taken 2 to 3 times a day, about 30 to 45 minutes before meals. Long-acting versions like Concerta are taken just once in the morning. Your doctor will usually start you on a low dose and slowly increase it until it works best for you. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
